verdict: Uber grew revenue 15% to $10.1B on 2.6 billion trips and made a small operating profit — but a $721M paper loss on its equity investments swung the bottom line to a $663M net loss.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs -$0.08 a year ago — hit by the investment loss below

segments.name: Mobility
segments.note: Rides — the original Uber business. Gross Bookings rose 25% to $18.7B; revenue growth was boosted by business-model changes in some countries.

segments.name: Delivery
segments.note: Food and grocery delivery — Uber Eats and couriers. Gross Bookings rose 18% to $17.7B.

segments.name: Freight
segments.note: Trucking logistics — matching shippers with carriers. Revenue fell 8% as a soft freight market cut revenue per load.

opex.name: Operations and support
opex.note: Running the platform day to day — support, operations and local teams.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Promotions, advertising and winning riders, eaters and drivers.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform and its autonomous-vehicle partnerships.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — legal, finance and the back office. This quarter it included $527M of legal, tax and regulatory reserve charges (see one-time items).

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of equipment and past acquisitions over their useful lives.

otherDetail: Other expense, net of $678M — including a $721M pre-tax loss from revaluing Uber's equity investments — plus $124M of interest expense and a $4M loss from equity method investments.
follow100Note: Of the $6.54 lost per $100 of revenue, $6.45 was the loss attributable to Uber shareholders and $0.09 belonged to non-controlling partners. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Net loss of $663M is the total including non-controlling interests; $654M is attributable to Uber shareholders (the -$0.32 EPS figure) because non-controlling partners absorbed a $9M loss. This was a net-loss quarter: the loss was covered by cash on Uber's balance sheet.

takeaways.title: The core business turned an operating profit
takeaways.text: Income from operations was $172M, up from a $262M loss a year ago, and Adjusted EBITDA jumped 82% to a record $1,382M as revenue growth outpaced costs.

takeaways.title: Bookings kept growing
takeaways.text: Gross Bookings rose 20% to $37.7B on 2.6 billion trips (+21%). Mobility revenue jumped 30% to $5,633M and Delivery rose 4% to $3,214M; Freight fell 8% to $1,284M in a soft trucking market.

takeaways.title: A paper loss flipped the bottom line to red
takeaways.text: Net loss was $663M only because Uber marked down the value of its equity investments by $721M (pre-tax) — a paper loss, not cash out the door. Free cash flow was $1,359M, up 148%.

oneTimers: Net loss includes a $721M pre-tax loss from net unrealized losses on the revaluation of Uber's equity investments — a paper loss that could reverse if those stocks rise.
General & administrative expense included $527M of legal, tax and regulatory reserve changes and settlements; excluding these and other items, non-GAAP G&A was $582M.
